thread.title: Microsoft (MSFT) 1st Quarter Earnings: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Microsoft (MSFT) 1st Quarter Earnings: What to Expect
text:
Microsoft (MSFT) 1st Quarter Earnings: What to Expect October 24, 2018, 08:20:35 AM EDT By Richard Saintvilus Shutterstock photo
Will cloud growth propel Microsoft ( MSFT ) stock towards all-time highs? And can the momentum help it join Apple ( AAPL ) and Amazon ( AMZN ) in the exclusive $1T market cap club?
These questions will be answered Wednesday when the world’s largest software company reports first quarter fiscal 2019 earnings results after the closing bell. Currently trading at around $110, MSFT stock has been on fire, rising 28% year to date, compared with a 3% rise for the S&P 500 index. The stock has been rewarded, thanks to a combination of factors. Namely, on the strength of the company’s cloud-first strategy which has emerged as a credible threat to Amazon’s AWS.
On Wednesday analyst will focus on the performance of Microsoft’s Intelligent Cloud services to assess if the growth momentum can continue into 2019.
For the quarter that ended September, the Redmond, Wash.-based tech giant is expected to earn 96 cents per share on revenue of $27.89 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earning were 84 cents per share on $24.54 billion in revenue. For the full year, ending June 2019, earnings are projected to rise 10.5% year over year to $4.29 per share, while full-year revenue of $122.93 billion would mark a year-over-year increase of 11.4%.
Wall Street is all in on Microsoft’s long-term growth prospects, thanks to the company’s strength in its Commercial Cloud business. In the fourth quarter, commercial cloud revenue, which consists of Office 365 commercial, Azure, and Dynamics 365, soared 35% year over year, which followed 58% jump in the third quarter. These gains contributed to consolidated revenue of $30.1 billion, up 17% year over year, topping not only the high end of the company's guidance but also Street estimates.
The bottom line was even more impressive, with profits raking in at $7.4 billion or $1.13 per share, surging 36% year over year and blowing past consensus estimates by five cents. Meanwhile, LinkedIn revenue, which is now tied to CEO Satya Nadella’s compensation , rose 34%, while user engagement surpassed 41%.
Once fully dependent on its Office and Windows franchises, Microsoft has fully transitioned towards faster-growing cloud business. The company several years ago set a goal to achieve a $20-billion run rate in its Commercial Cloud business. What was once considered a "a pipe dream" among the analyst community is now seen as a foregone conclusion to the point where some analysts believe Microsoft Azure — posting an 89% year-over-year growth rate — will eventually overtake Amazon as the top cloud platform.
Nonetheless, while the company is posting strong revenue and profit growth and seemingly operating on all cylinders, on Wednesday Wall Street will want to see evidence that the company’s cloud growth can continue to accelerate into 2019. At that point its shares will confidently rise towards the $1T market cap.
